primary_claim: Introspective awareness (detecting injected concept vectors) is a behaviorally robust capability that is absent in base models, emerges specifically from contrastive preference-optimization post-training such as DPO (not SFT), is implemented by a distributed two-stage 'evidence carrier'/'gate' MLP circuit rather than a single linear direction, and is substantially underelicited by default.

effect.metric: true positive detection rate (TPR) after refusal-direction ablation
effect.value: 10.8% to 63.8% (introspection rate 4.6% to 24.1%), with FPR rising only 0.0% to 7.3%

contradicts_or_qualifies: Godet (2025a) raised concerns that steering generically biases models toward 'Yes' answers; the authors show detection cannot be explained by a single linear direction, addressing this
Findings are difficult to reconcile with the hypothesis that models report detection merely as a pretext to discuss the injected concept
limitations_stated: Majority of experiments conducted on Gemma3-27B; more capable or differently-trained models may show qualitatively different introspection patterns
Strategic behaviors like sandbagging or sycophancy might confound measurement in ways the methodology would not detect
Do not evaluate architectures besides transformer-based LLMs
Behavioral metrics rely on LLM judge classification, which may introduce systematic biases
Mechanistic interpretability tooling for open-source models remains limited; role of attention in the circuit remains unclear
quote: Ablating refusal directions improves detection by +53% and a trained bias vector improves detection by +75% on held-out concepts, both without meaningfully increasing false positives.
